subject: Post-demo recap: token profile, budget range & target $/1M
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah@medlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: token profile, budget range & target $/1M

Hi Sarah — thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we don’t lose momentum.

Call highlights:
- Workload: clinical notes summarization + EHR QA (mostly short-to-medium context, 200–1,000 tokens per request).
- Expected cadence: bursty at end of month, baseline steady state ~120k requests/day.
- Monthly token estimate: ~350M input tokens + ~150M generated tokens ≈ 500M tokens/month.
- SLA needs: 99.9% availability for core API routes, data residency in us-west preferred.

Cost/price qualification (what we need from you):
1) Budget range you’re thinking for inference (monthly) — ballpark is OK (you said procurement needs a range).
2) Target $/1M tokens threshold for evaluation — you mentioned an internal target earlier; can you confirm a target band (e.g., $30–$80 / 1M)?
3) Pilot acceptance criteria — latency SLOs, throughput, and quality checks (we’ll map to prompts).

What we’ll send next (by Monday):
- A short pilot pricing sheet with 4 options (hosted pilot, dedicated pilot, burst-enabled, and quantized model variant).
- A one-sheet benchmarking snapshot vs OpenAI/Anthropic and two large open-model hosts (1M token cost comparisons).
- Draft mutual action plan with milestones and success metrics.

Next steps: can we lock a 30-minute procurement intro next week (proposed slots: Tue 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 14:00–15:00 PT)? I’ll include Ben for pricing specifics and Monica for onboarding/CS.

Thanks — looking forward.

— Priyom

From: Sarah Chen <sarah@medlytics.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 17:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: token profile, budget range & target $/1M

On Fri, May 25, 2028 at 2:12 PM Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Sarah — thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we don’t lose momentum.

Thanks, Priyom — that summary is accurate. A few clarifications from our side:

- Monthly budget: we’re budgeting at the portfolio level for this team. For a POC/pilot we can commit up to $12k/month. If the pilot shows clear unit-econ improvements, procurement has authority to expand to $75k/month for production in Q4.
- Target $/1M: our internal goal is to get to <= $45 / 1M tokens for the production run. For the pilot we can accept higher per-1M to validate quality and latency (up to ~$120 / 1M).
- Volumes for pilot: we prefer a phased pilot — start with a 30-day sandbox at ~15M tokens, then 90-day pilot at ~120M tokens if all metrics pass.
- Primary constraints: must pass our security checklist (SOC2 evidence + audit logs) and support redaction for PHI in transit.

Procurement (James) will be looped for formal review — I’ve cc’d him. Happy to take Tue 10am PT.

— Sarah
Sarah Chen
Head of Data Products, MedLytics
sarah@medlytics.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 26 May 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: token profile, budget range & target $/1M

Priyom / Monica — quick internal:

Great signal on MedLytics’ target of <= $45/1M for production and pilot tolerance up to $120/1M. Given their pilot sizing (15M -> 120M), recommended approach:

1) Pilot pricing structure (attached 'pilot-pricing-sheet.csv'):
   - Sandbox (30d, 15M): $115 / 1M (fully hosted, priority infra) — flat fee + overage model to keep commitment low.
   - Phase 2 (90d, 120M): tiered volume pricing with $55 / 1M at committed 120M; option to add dedicated capacity if sustained.
   - Long-term production target: offer a migration path to $42 / 1M if they commit to 12-month reserved capacity (or equivalent consumption).

2) Competitive benchmark (attached 'host-comps-1M.xlsx') — I prepared a conservative 1M token cost comparison vs OpenAI (gpt-4x) and Anthropic (claude-advanced) and two open-hosts. Key takeaway: open-host pricing varies widely at scale; we can be positioned between Anthropic and low-cost open-hosts while delivering better SLA/observability for healthcare.

3) Compliance ask: Monica, can you prep a SOC2 evidence packet + PHI redaction notes for the Tue call? Also list which redwood agents can be scoped out for PII/PHI handling.

I’ll join Tue 10am and handle pricing walk. Priyom, if you want, I can slide in a conservative counter-offer to anchor closer to $60/1M for Phase 2 and then take to leadership for the $42/1M reserved ask.

— Ben
Ben Carter | Account Lead, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0149
